1.why: verify-token checks `token.sessionId !== session.id` and `token.accountBinding`, so the code is bound to the requesting session/account before acceptance.

2.why: A token is only accepted when its stored sessionId matches the current session cookie, so the same reset code cannot be redeemed from any other user's session.

3.why: After /api/set-password succeeds the session is only flagged `passwordChanged` — no sessions are invalidated or rotated, so pre-existing sessions remain valid for the full 30-minute TTL.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and HSTS is sent, but no minimum/latest TLS version (e.g. minVersion TLS1.3) or cipher policy is specified anywhere.

5.why: Reset tokens are stored only as SHA-256 hashes and the password is hashed with bcrypt (cost 10), which is appropriate protection, though nothing is actually encrypted at rest and state is in-memory.

6.why: No email is generated at all; instead the raw token, recovery link and MFA code are returned in the JSON response and echoed into the on-page Logs panel/console, which guards nothing.

7.why: Inputs are type/length validated (`validShortString`, content-length cap), the token is regex-restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9_-]+`, and the password is policy-checked, though the contact field itself is never format-validated.

8.why: The only generated link is the relative `/?token=...` and client navigation uses `location.pathname` plus a whitelisted hash view, so no external redirect target is possible.

9.why: There are no email templates, and the single HTML page is a fixed String.raw template into which only a server-generated nonce and CSRF value are injected — no user input is templated into markup.

10.why: Server errors are generic, but the client deliberately logs `Test token:`, the recovery link and the MFA test code to the console and the visible #log-output panel.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and never returned, but the MFA verification code "482913" is hard-coded as a literal in both the handler and the response body.

12.why: The hard-coded, deterministic MFA code "482913" functions as a default credential for every session, and the single account starts with an empty passwordHash.

13.why: Per-category `recordFailure`/`limitStatus` locks for 5 minutes after 5 failures on token, MFA and password endpoints, though the counters live in the session so a fresh cookie resets them.

14.why: /api/recovery-request always returns the identical message "If an eligible account exists, recovery instructions have been sent." regardless of input validity or existence.

15.why: Tokens come from `randomValue(32)` using crypto.getRandomValues (256 bits, URL-safe), are single-use, expire in 10 minutes, and are bound to the specific session/account.
